claim: The agent set the campaign's measurement order as a coarse gate map first (the cheapest stacking discriminator), then a Landau fan as an independent band-structure/pocket-count check, with the temperature ladder run last because the cooldown after it is passive and slow.
context: Immediately after bring-up and reading the device and rig cards, before any sweep had run, the agent wrote a plan ranking the three candidate measurements by cost and discriminating power.
evidence: Written plan citing the discriminators: neutrality-resistance magnitude/displacement-field dependence from a gate map, SdH tone count from a Landau fan, and an Arrhenius gap Delta(D) from a temperature ladder run last.

claim: During the first back-gate liveness cut, the Rxx lock-in channel clipped (full-scale fraction just above 1.0, pinned above about 218 ohm) over roughly the last third of the sweep, while the drain-current channel stayed unclipped throughout.
context: The agent was watching the first rows of the initial back-gate sweep live and flagged the clipping as it appeared, comparing the two lock-in channels' full-scale fractions in real time.
evidence: Drain current flat ~9.9->9.87 nA (fs 0.50); Rxx channel fs 1.09, clipping over roughly 30% of the sweep once the full trace landed.

claim: The agent concluded that under this high-impedance current bias, the drain current cannot serve as a charge-neutrality locator, because a ~100 megohm bias resistor makes the current only weakly sensitive to channel resistance until the channel resistance approaches the bias resistor's own value.
context: Comparing the nearly flat drain-current trace against the clipped Rxx trace from the same liveness cut, the agent reasoned from the bias-resistor value and the fractional current change to explain why the current-based neutrality dip was almost invisible.
evidence: Predicted ~0.1% current change for a 100 ohm to 100 kilohm channel-resistance swing under a 100 megohm bias resistor; observed current dip only ~0.7%, attributed instead to contact resistance.

claim: The agent changed the Rxx lock-in's sensitivity from 2 microvolt (clipping) to 1 millivolt and lowered the time constant on both lock-ins from 0.3 s to 0.1 s, cutting the compliant per-point dwell from ~2.1 s to ~0.7 s for every subsequent sweep.
context: After the first liveness cut clipped the Rxx channel and made the compliant dwell expensive, the agent requested this acquisition-configuration change, received operator authorization, and executed it before repeating the cut.
evidence: New sensitivity gives ~100 kilohm of Rxx headroom at the 10 nA bias current; 24 dB/oct filter still keeps the second harmonic ~99 dB down at the drive frequency with the shorter time constant.

claim: The repeat back-gate liveness cut was swept in reverse (from the positive end back down) relative to the first pass, letting the agent get a hysteresis check between the two sweeps at no extra cost.
context: Immediately after re-ranging the acquisition, the agent designed the second back-gate cut to start where the first one had parked the gate and sweep back the other way.
evidence: Run 1 swept opposite in direction to run 0; the two were later compared and found to differ by about one grid step (50 mV) of hysteresis.

claim: The re-ranged, unclipped back-gate cut located the charge-neutrality point at V_bg = -0.250 V (top gate at 0 V), with a neutrality-point resistance there of 297 ohm.
context: With the lock-in no longer clipping, the agent read the peak of the Rxx trace directly off the repeated back-gate sweep to fix the charge-neutrality point that every later sweep would be designed around.
evidence: Peak Rxx = 297 ohm at V_bg = -0.250 V; used to derive an intrinsic-doping offset (~+3.8e11 cm^-2) and a near-zero displacement field at that crossing.

claim: The agent inferred that two-terminal contact resistance, not the channel, dominates the drain-current dip seen near neutrality, estimating roughly 0.4 megohm of resistance per contact that roughly doubles through the neutrality point.
context: Comparing the two-terminal resistance implied by the drain-current dip against the much smaller four-terminal Rxx from the same runs, the agent used the ratio to argue the probe contacts were responsible for most of the two-terminal signal.
evidence: R_2t ~0.75 megohm off-neutrality vs. four-terminal Rxx ~100 ohm; a companion ~7-10% probe-loading systematic on absolute Rxx cited from the lock-in's 10 megohm input impedance.

claim: The agent flagged a double-peaked structure near neutrality seen in one of the two back-gate cuts as ambiguous, proposing it reflects either two slightly differently doped regions between the voltage probes or genuine multi-band structure at neutrality, and deferred judgment to the upcoming gate map's many neutrality crossings.
context: The double peak, about ten times the noise floor, appeared only in the unclipped cut, since the other cut's clipping had erased that part of the trace, so the agent could not yet tell which explanation applied.
evidence: Two peaks (297 ohm and ~272 ohm) with a ~35% dip between them, well above the ~3% per-point noise floor, seen in a single sweep only.

claim: The agent initially concluded that a several-percent, point-to-point wiggle common to the two back-gate cuts was reproducible physical structure rather than instrument noise.
context: Overlaying the two back-gate cuts and seeing them track closely outside the clipped region, the agent's first read was that the shared wiggle pattern must be a real, reproducible feature of the device.
evidence: Point-by-point overlay of the two cuts in the unclipped region, described as agreeing 'point-for-point' with a shared wiggle of roughly 12%.

claim: For the coarse gate map, the agent swept the back gate across its full negative range but stopped the positive side at +0.40 V, well short of the card limit, once it determined the charge-neutrality line exits the accessible top-gate window there, and put the freed sweep budget into finer step resolution instead.
context: Using the back-gate/top-gate neutrality relation just measured from the second liveness cut, the agent computed where the neutrality line leaves the accessible top-gate window and cut the slow-axis range there before launching the two-dimensional map.
evidence: Neutrality line V_bg = -1.158*V_tg - 0.250 leaves the top-gate window at V_bg ~ +0.10 V; rows above that judged to carry no neutrality crossing and to cost ~25 extra minutes for no stacking information.

claim: After the first attempt at the gate map crashed at the third of 2310 points, the agent diagnosed the cause as an added live two-dimensional plot and relaunched the identical sweep with only that plot removed, changing no measurement parameter.
context: The sweep died with a broken-pipe error from the plotting subprocess; the agent traced it to an O(N^2) re-interpolation the added live map performed on every point, and chose to fix the plotting rather than alter the measurement.
evidence: Crash traceback pointed at the added 2D live-plot call; two earlier, successful 1D-only-plotted sweeps (runs 0 and 1) confirmed the 2D live plot as the sole difference.

claim: The agent retracted its earlier claim of reproducible structure, finding after comparing the run-to-run difference against the noise-only prediction that the wiggle is essentially all lock-in noise, with only a small residual (about two per cent) unexplained.
context: Before letting the first read stand in the analysis notebook, the agent recomputed the expected purely-random run-to-run difference from the per-point noise and compared it to the observed difference between the two back-gate cuts.
evidence: Observed run-to-run rms difference ~4.5 ohm vs. noise-only prediction ~3.8 ohm; per-point sigma 2.2-3.2 ohm, consistent with SR830 1/f noise at the ~13.8 Hz drive frequency.

claim: Across the full gate map, the neutrality-point resistance rose steeply with displacement field but then flattened to a plateau of roughly 3 kilohm above a displacement field around 0.23 V/nm, rather than continuing to rise.
context: Once the coarse gate map completed, the agent extracted the neutrality-point resistance along the fitted charge-neutrality line as a function of displacement field and noticed the high-field rows no longer followed the steep initial trend.
evidence: Per-row neutrality peak values plateauing near ~3 kilohm above D/eps0 ~ 0.23 V/nm, versus a steep rise below it.

claim: The gate map showed the neutrality-point resistance rising by a factor of 10.4 as displacement field increased, from 296 ohm near zero field to 3074 ohm at the map's largest displacement field (D/eps0 ~ +0.31 V/nm).
context: This was extracted after the gate map finished, by fitting the neutrality-point resistance along the measured charge-neutrality line across roughly 30 line crossings in the two-dimensional dataset.
evidence: Neutrality resistance 296 ohm (D~0) to 3074 ohm (D/eps0 = +0.307-0.31 V/nm).

claim: The agent concluded that the ~10x, displacement-field-driven rise in neutrality-point resistance rules out a band-overlapped semimetallic (Bernal-type) stacking, since such a stacking's overlapping bands should keep the neutrality point conducting under displacement field.
context: This conclusion rested directly on the gate map's measured neutrality-resistance-vs-field trend, reasoned against the expected band physics of a band-overlapped semimetal.
evidence: 10.4x rise (296 ohm to 3074 ohm) used as an exclusionary argument against the semimetallic candidate stacking.

claim: The minimum of the neutrality-point resistance across the gate map sat at D/eps0 = 0.000 +/- 0.008 V/nm, with the resistance folded about that minimum agreeing between positive and negative displacement field to within about seven per cent.
context: The agent located the argmin of the fitted neutrality-resistance-vs-field curve with a parabolic fit on the log-resistance data, then folded the curve about that minimum to compare the two field-sign branches.
evidence: Argmin at D/eps0 = 0.000+/-0.008 V/nm; folded-branch ratios of 1.07, 1.01, 1.03, 0.96 at |dD| = 0.02-0.08 V/nm, against a ~3% per-point noise floor.

claim: The agent inferred that the neutrality-resistance minimum sitting at zero displacement field, with the two field-sign branches folding onto each other, demonstrates inversion symmetry of the stack and disfavors a stacking that lacks inversion symmetry, whose built-in gap would displace the minimum to finite field.
context: This inference was drawn directly from the located minimum and its robustness to the calibration uncertainty on the measured gate-capacitance ratio.
evidence: Displacement of the minimum under +/-1 sigma capacitance-ratio uncertainty found to be under 0.001 V/nm, negligible against the measured 0.000+/-0.008 V/nm minimum location.

claim: The gate map's own charge-neutrality-line slope gave a top-gate-to-back-gate capacitance ratio of 1.2737 +/- 0.0470, about ten per cent higher than the geometry-based prior (1.1579) the session started with, and this measured ratio was adopted for every later cut or sweep needing the displacement-field axis.
context: The agent fit the neutrality line across about 26 unambiguous rows of the completed gate map to extract the capacitance ratio, comparing it to the prior computed from the stated gate-stack thicknesses.
evidence: Measured ratio 1.2737+/-0.0470 vs. geometry prior 1.1579, about 2 sigma apart.

claim: The agent interpreted the neutrality-resistance plateau above D/eps0 ~ 0.23 V/nm as inconsistent with a cleanly growing single-particle gap, proposing a parallel conduction path or disorder-induced in-gap states as the more likely explanation, and flagged that this makes the planned activation measurement (rather than resistance itself) the more trustworthy route to a gap value.
context: Because a genuine single-particle gap should keep driving resistance up exponentially with field, the plateau in the gate map's neutrality-resistance curve above ~0.23 V/nm looked to the agent like a floor set by some other conduction channel.
evidence: Plateau near ~3 kilohm above D/eps0~0.23 V/nm instead of continued exponential rise.

claim: For the Landau fan, the agent swept field from 0.75 T up to a 6 T ceiling (well under the session's field cap), upward once without retracing, with the density axis co-swept along the just-measured charge-neutrality line from n = -1.04e12 to +2.10e12 cm^-2, centered on neutrality so both carrier signs were covered.
context: The agent designed this sweep as an independent, calibration-light test of the band structure once the gate map had established the gap physics, sizing the field ceiling against how much extra time each additional field increment would cost given the magnet's fixed ramp rate.
evidence: Chosen ceiling 6 T (not the session's full field cap); density window centered at the measured charge-neutrality-line crossing (CNP at V_tg=-0.003); grid uniform in inverse field for the planned frequency analysis.

claim: When proposing the Landau fan, the agent claimed that a rhombohedral four-layer stack's Landau-level degeneracy (a single 16-fold-degenerate zero-energy level, giving first flanking gaps at filling factor +/-8) would look visibly different from a Bernal-stacked four-layer's Landau-level sequence, and that counting filling factors alone would settle the stacking order.
context: This claim was made in the sweep's own design write-up, before the fan's data existed, as the primary physical justification for measuring the Landau fan at all.
evidence: Stated degeneracy argument: rhombohedral tetralayer 4x4=16 states at nu=+/-8 vs. a Bernal tetralayer's two-bilayer decomposition giving 'a visibly different sequence.'

claim: The agent decided, as a standing contingency, that if session time grew tight it would shorten the planned field down-sweep rather than the temperature ladder, judging the activation measurement the higher-value use of remaining time.
context: This priority call was made while costing the remaining plan (down-sweep, then temperature ladder, then close-out), reasoning that the gate map's resistance plateau made the activation gap the more informative remaining measurement.
evidence: Explicit statement that the down-sweep would be shortened before the ladder if time became tight.

claim: For the activation ladder, the agent chose seven temperature setpoints ascending from base (~1.2 K) through 8, 12, 17, 23, 30, and 40 K, each measured with a co-swept multisweep tracing five parallel offsets (0, +/-0.05, +/-0.10 V) around the fitted charge-neutrality line, and accepted each temperature once it had stabilized rather than once it was merely close to setpoint.
context: Designed before the fan and down-sweep had finished so it could launch immediately once the field returned to zero, this sweep let the neutrality-point resistance be read as the maximum over several offset traces at each temperature, guarding against the fitted line or the neutrality point drifting as the sample warmed.
evidence: Seven temperatures via a fixed heater-ratio protocol (ratio 0.95); five perpendicular offsets per temperature; stability-based (not proximity-based) acceptance, motivated by the sample loop's known overshoot and slow recovery.

claim: While the Landau fan was running and the neutrality-column resistance was climbing fast enough to be about to exceed the lock-in's range, the agent chose not to re-range the sensitivity, judging the resulting loss of the neutrality column's magnitude cheaper than losing the finite-density quantum-oscillation minima the current sensitivity was tuned for.
context: At a mid-run checkpoint the agent projected the neutrality column would clip within about another half tesla and weighed re-ranging against the fan's actual purpose, the Landau-level sequence and pocket count away from neutrality.
evidence: Neutrality-column resistance climbing through several kilohm per 0.1 T step near the checkpoint (6.6k to 14.1k ohm between 0.84 and 0.97 T); finite-density minima already resolved down to a few ohm under the current sensitivity.

claim: Rather than a bare ramp back to zero field after the fan, the agent measured through the mandatory ramp-down as a second field sweep from 6 T down to 0.5 T over 100 points, at five fixed densities (n = -0.8, +0.5, +1.0, +1.5, +2.0 x10^12 cm^-2) along the neutrality line, extending the field baseline to raise the frequency resolution (0.55 T) and Nyquist limit (27.3 T) for counting Fermi-surface tones.
context: The agent recognized the ramp back to zero (needed before the zero-field activation ladder) as otherwise-wasted fridge time and designed a sweep to use it, motivated by the fan's own analysis showing its highest-density columns would alias in a frequency spectrum.
evidence: Descending 1/B-uniform grid, 6 T to 0.5 T, 100 points; stated resolution 0.55 T and Nyquist 27.3 T, comfortably above the ~20.7 T maximum expected Onsager frequency in the density window.

claim: For the field down-sweep, the agent deliberately left the lock-in sensitivity at the same 1 mV setting used in the fan, accepting that the n=+0.50e12 cm^-2 density trace would likely clip near its resistance peaks rather than coarsen the range and destroy the oscillation minima that carry the pocket-count signal.
context: This was an explicit trade-off stated while validating the down-sweep design, prioritizing the low-resistance oscillation minima over full resolution of one trace's peak values.
evidence: Anticipated clipping on the n=+0.50e12 cm^-2 trace near its Landau-filling-factor ~3.4 peak at 6 T; the fan itself had already shown oscillation minima reaching only a few ohm.

claim: The agent found the magnet's actual measured field running about +6.5 mT above its commanded setpoint at the fan's starting field, with an additional ~2 mT of point-to-point spread within a row (~0.9% at 0.75 T), confirming the setpoint could not stand in for the true field.
context: While the Landau fan was running, the agent caught an analysis bug that had been reading the commanded setpoint column instead of the measured field column, and on fixing it compared the two directly from the raw sweep record.
evidence: Measured field +6.5 mT above setpoint at 0.75 T, ~2 mT within-row spread; traced to a helper function silently resolving a duplicate column name to the setpoint rather than the followed readback.

claim: From the Landau fan's minima, the agent found a uniform filling-factor spacing consistent with the standard four-fold spin-valley degeneracy, and adopted that degeneracy (over two-fold or eight-fold alternatives) because it gives the most physically plausible top-gate dielectric thickness (11.1 nm vs. the ~9.5 nm stated for the stack) relative to the two-fold (~22 nm, implausible) and eight-fold (~5.5 nm, unlikely) alternatives, while noting this assumption is not needed for the stacking call itself.
context: The agent compared three possible Landau-level degeneracies against the fan's measured minima spacing and the resulting implied gate capacitance, checking each against the nominal gate-stack thickness for plausibility.
evidence: Minima spacing uniform to within a few per cent across ten flanking levels; degeneracy g=4 implying c_tg=2.40 mF/m^2 (11.1 nm equivalent hBN) judged plausible against the ~9.5 nm stated stack.

claim: The Landau fan's frequency spectrum carried a single tone scaling linearly with density through the origin (r~0.996 after excluding one column near the frequency-resolution edge), sitting at roughly 0.84x the full Onsager frequency for one carrier pocket, while secondary spectral peaks showed no such trend (r~-0.15).
context: The agent fit the dominant spectral peak's frequency against density across the fan's density columns, after catching and excluding one column whose peak-picking had failed right at the fan's frequency-resolution edge.
evidence: Linear fit through origin, r=0.996, slope 8.72 T per 10^12 cm^-2 (0.84x full-Onsager slope); secondary peaks 4.2, 9.7, 9.1, 2.6, 8.4, 4.6 T show no monotonic trend.

claim: The agent concluded that a single density-scaling spectral tone in the Landau fan, with no second tone tracking density, is the signature of a single quartic Fermi pocket rather than two separate bilayer-like pockets, disfavoring the semimetallic (Bernal-type) stacking whose two bands should both produce density-scaling tones.
context: This conclusion followed directly from the single linear tone found in the fan's frequency-vs-density fit, contrasted with the two-tone signature expected from a stacking with two bands crossing the Fermi level at neutrality field.
evidence: One tone tracking density (r~0.996); no second density-scaling tone found among the remaining spectral peaks.

claim: The agent retracted its earlier Landau-level-degeneracy argument, concluding instead that the zero-energy Landau level's degeneracy scales with the number of layers regardless of stacking order (4N, i.e. 16 states for either tetralayer candidate), so filling-factor counting alone cannot distinguish the two stackings.
context: Working through the Landau-level physics needed to interpret the fan's minima spacing, the agent found its original justification for the fan (that filling-factor counting would separate the candidates) was physically wrong, and recorded the correction alongside the fan's actual, still-valid contribution (the pocket count).
evidence: Semimetallic four-layer stack shown to decompose into two effective bilayers, each with an 8-state zero level (all at exactly zero energy), summing to the same 16 states as the rhombohedral candidate; correction also entered as an erratum in the measurement notebook.

claim: In the higher-resolution field down-sweep, four of the five fixed-density traces returned exactly one unflagged spectral tone each, and the two highest-contrast traces gave a tone frequency at essentially the same fraction (0.835 and 0.834) of the full expected cyclotron frequency for one carrier pocket.
context: The agent re-ran the tone-finding analysis on the down-sweep, specifically designed with enough frequency resolution and Nyquist range to avoid the fan's aliasing problem, and compared the resulting tone count and frequency ratio across densities.
evidence: Tone-frequency ratios 0.835 and 0.834 for the two highest-contrast (n=+0.99, +1.49 x10^12 cm^-2) traces; linear fit through origin over |n|>0.9 giving 8.62 T per 10^12 cm^-2 against a 10.34 T/10^12cm^-2 full-Onsager slope.

claim: The absolute density-scale correction implied by the down-sweep's tone ratio (alpha=1.199) agreed with the equivalent correction implied by the Landau fan's independent minima-ladder spacing (alpha=1.166) to within about 2.8 per cent, despite being separate datasets and separate analysis routes.
context: The agent compared the density-scale factor extracted from the down-sweep's tone frequency against the one extracted earlier from the fan's Landau-level minima spacing.
evidence: alpha=1.199 (down-sweep tone) vs. alpha=1.166 (fan minima ladder), agreeing to 2.8%.

claim: The agent concluded that the down-sweep's one-tone-per-density result, needing no absolute density calibration to interpret, confirms the single-Fermi-pocket picture from the fan and further disfavors the semimetallic (Bernal-type) stacking, whose two bilayer-like bands should each contribute a density-scaling tone.
context: This inference rested on the down-sweep's higher-resolution, alias-free tone count, treated by the agent as the more decisive of the two pocket-counting measurements because it needed no calibration assumption.
evidence: No density trace returning two density-scaling tones; consistent single-tone result across four of five densities.

claim: The agent initially stated that every one of the five fixed-density traces in the field down-sweep yielded exactly one unflagged spectral tone.
context: This was the agent's first summary read of the down-sweep's tone-finding output across all five density traces.
evidence: Summary statement that 'every density yields exactly one unflagged tone.'

claim: The agent corrected its own summary, noting that the n=+1.99x10^12 cm^-2 trace actually returned no unflagged tone at all (all candidates flagged marginal or harmonic), so the true result is four of five densities gave a single clean tone, not all five.
context: On rereading the tone-finder's output more carefully, the agent caught that its prior 'every density' summary overstated the result for one of the five traces.
evidence: n=+1.99x10^12 cm^-2 trace's tones all flagged marginal or harmonic, yielding no usable frequency.

claim: The agent noted that the down-sweep's pocket-count result cannot exclude a small second Fermi pocket carrying under roughly ten per cent of the carriers, because a tone from such a pocket would fall at a low frequency (below ~1.5 T) that the polynomial background-removal step used before the spectral fit would remove along with the background.
context: This caveat was recorded alongside the down-sweep's one-tone read, explicitly limiting how strong a two-pocket exclusion the measurement can support.
evidence: Degree-5 polynomial background removal stated to be capable of absorbing a low-frequency tone (<1.5 T) from a small satellite pocket.

claim: At the neutrality point closest to zero displacement field, the neutrality-point resistance rose with increasing temperature across the ladder (249 ohm at 1.2 K to 360 ohm at 40 K), giving a fitted activation energy of -0.62 +/- 0.17 meV, consistent with metallic behavior.
context: The agent fit an Arrhenius form to the neutrality-point resistance versus measured sample temperature at each of the seven ladder points, restricted to temperatures at or above the sample's own electron temperature (~8 K).
evidence: Delta = -0.62+/-0.17 meV; R_CNP 249 ohm (1.2 K, excluded from fit) rising to 360 ohm (40 K).

claim: At the ladder's largest displacement field (D/eps0 = +0.238 V/nm), the neutrality-point resistance fell with increasing temperature (2975 ohm to 1175 ohm), giving a fitted activation energy of +1.36 +/- 0.14 meV, consistent with insulating behavior.
context: The same Arrhenius fit procedure applied at a much larger displacement field than the D~0 column gave the opposite sign of activation energy.
evidence: Delta = +1.36+/-0.14 meV; R_CNP 2975 ohm falling to 1175 ohm across the fitted temperature range.

claim: The sign of the neutrality-point resistance's temperature dependence flipped at D/eps0 = +0.126 V/nm, and all seven of the ladder's temperature isotherms crossed the neutrality-resistance-vs-displacement-field curves at that same single field value, with the insulating flank rising at 7.9 meV per V/nm.
context: The agent overlaid the seven temperature isotherms of neutrality resistance versus displacement field and located the common crossing point where the metallic and insulating trends meet.
evidence: Common crossing at D/eps0=+0.126 V/nm across all seven isotherms; +D flank slope 7.9 meV per V/nm.

claim: The agent judged the displacement-field-driven crossover from metallic to insulating behavior at the neutrality point as the cleanest disqualification in the session of the band-overlapped semimetallic (Bernal-type) stacking, since such a stacking's overlapping bands should keep the neutrality point metallic at every displacement field.
context: This was drawn directly from the activation ladder's sign-flipping temperature dependence, treated as independent confirmation of the gap-opening conclusion already reached from the gate map's resistance rise.
evidence: Sign change of the fitted activation energy from -0.62 meV to +1.36 meV with increasing displacement field.

claim: The agent's first attempt at testing the activation gap for inversion symmetry extrapolated a straight-line fit of the positive-displacement-field flank back to zero field, obtaining an intercept of about -1.12 meV that did not correspond to a physically meaningful zero-field gap.
context: Before recognizing the curved shape of the gap-vs-displacement-field curve, the agent tried a linear extrapolation of the higher-field activation data as its first inversion-symmetry test.
evidence: Linear-intercept extrapolation returning -1.12 meV, later described by the agent as meaningless.

claim: Recognizing that the activation gap is visibly curved (parabolic) near its minimum rather than linear, the agent instead fit a parabola to the ~29 points around the minimum and located the gap's zero-crossing displacement field at D = +0.016 +/- 0.004 V/nm.
context: The agent replaced its earlier linear-extrapolation approach, judging it the wrong statistic for a curved function, and refit the same activation dataset with the correct functional form.
evidence: Parabolic fit over ~29 points giving minimum-gap displacement field +0.016+/-0.004 V/nm.

claim: The agent judged the measured activation gap's magnitude (1.36 meV at D/eps0~0.25 V/nm) to be one to two orders of magnitude below what a clean single-particle band gap should give at that displacement field, and concluded (together with the gate map's resistance plateau) that transport is limited by disorder or a parallel conduction channel, so this measurement establishes the gap's existence and D-dependence but not its true size.
context: Comparing the fitted activation energy at the ladder's largest displacement field against the expected scale of a genuine single-particle gap at that field, the agent concluded the transport-derived gap value should not be read as the band gap itself.
evidence: Delta_max=1.36 meV judged one to two orders of magnitude below an expected clean single-particle gap; cited alongside the gate map's ~3 kilohm resistance-plateau finding.

claim: The agent noted a tension between the two independent estimates of where the gap minimum sits -- 0.000+/-0.008 V/nm from base-temperature resistance vs. +0.016+/-0.004 V/nm from activation, a difference several times the smaller estimate's own fit uncertainty -- but concluded this should not be read as evidence for a stacking lacking inversion symmetry, since both estimates sit within a few per cent of the accessible displacement-field range from zero.
context: This tension was flagged explicitly in the final write-up comparing the two independently derived minimum-gap locations, one from resistance alone and one from the temperature-dependence fit.
evidence: Minimum locations 0.000+/-0.008 V/nm (resistance, run 3) vs. +0.016+/-0.004 V/nm (activation, runs 6-12).

claim: The agent's final stacking-order call for the only wired four-terminal region was rhombohedral-type, at moderate (not strong) confidence, based on four converging lines of evidence: a 10.4x displacement-field-driven gap at neutrality, a gap minimum centered on zero displacement field, a displacement-field-driven metal-to-insulator crossover at neutrality, and a single Fermi pocket.
context: This verdict was written at session close after all planned measurements (two gate cuts, the gate map, the Landau fan, the field down-sweep, and the seven-point temperature ladder) had completed and been analyzed, explicitly excluding a band-overlapped semimetallic stacking on two independent grounds and disfavoring an inversion-asymmetric stacking on the basis of the gap-minimum location.
evidence: 10.4x neutrality-resistance rise; gap minimum at 0.000+/-0.008 V/nm (resistance) and +0.016+/-0.004 V/nm (activation); metal-insulator sign flip in activation energy; single density-scaling SdH tone in two independent field sweeps (fan and down-sweep). Confidence held to 'moderate' chiefly because the negative-displacement-field lever arm was only about a quarter of the positive one (limited by the top-gate card limit), and the measured activation gap's magnitude (1.36 meV) is well below a clean single-particle scale.

claim: The agent left the third (silicon) gate untouched at 0.000 V for the entire session and, at close-out, chose only to read and report it rather than ramp it, reasoning that the graphite back gate already screens it from the channel so it carried no needed information this session.
context: This scope decision was recorded in the hand-authored close-out cell, noting that ramping this gate requires separate authorization that was not sought.
evidence: Silicon gate held at 0.000 V for the whole session; close-out cell explicitly declines to ramp it and instead flags it for the operator.

claim: For shutdown, the agent chose to turn the heaters off first (so the sample would begin cooling immediately), then ramp both active gates to zero at a fixed 5 mV/step pace, and only then ramp the field to zero, rather than doing these in parallel or a different order.
context: This ordering was written into the hand-authored close-out cell to start the slowest process -- cooling from the ladder's highest temperature -- as early as possible.
evidence: Close-out cell's stated order: heaters off, then gate ramp to zero at 5 mV/step, then field ramp to zero, then a full instrument readback.

claim: In its first, hand-authored close-out, the agent deliberately did not restore the lock-in sensitivity and time-constant settings to their session-start values, reasoning that the session-start values had been wrong for this device and restoring them would hand the next session a known-bad acquisition configuration.
context: This choice was stated explicitly in the hand-authored close-out cell, before the operator later required the canonical restore-to-initial-state helper instead.
evidence: Session-start lock-in sensitivity (2 microvolt) had been railed at the device's zero-gate operating point; the session's working values (1 mV sensitivity, 0.1 s time constant) were left in place instead.

claim: At the operator's explicit instruction, the agent ran the canonical restore-to-captured-state close-out helper instead of its own hand-written version, which restored the lock-ins to their session-start sensitivity (2 microvolt) and time constant (0.3 s) -- reintroducing the configuration that had been clipping at the start of the session -- and set the field endpoint explicitly to 0.0 T rather than leaving it implicit.
